s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of joint pain and swelling following medical treatment for a gynecological condition
salient_findings: Diffuse swelling and tenderness to palpation of both knees
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: 6 weeks of amenorrhea
Right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Vaginal bleeding
Empty uterine cavity on transvaginal ultrasonography
Gestational sac in the right adnexa without fetal cardiac activity
Initial serum β-hCG level of 585 mIU/mL
Decline in β-hCG level after methotrexate treatment
Pain and swelling in both knees after methotrexate treatment
Diffuse swelling and tenderness to palpation of both knees
Elevated white-cell count
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Elevated C-reactive protein level
Joint ultrasonography revealed anterior soft-tissue swelling with a thickened synovium and fluid collections

shortlist.label: Methotrexate-induced rheumatologic reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed joint pain and swelling after methotrexate treatment

shortlist.label: Reactive arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a recent history of gynecological treatment and now presents with joint pain and swelling

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated white-cell count, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and C-reactive protein level, which could indicate a septic process

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with diffuse swelling and tenderness to palpation of both knees, which could be indicative of an autoimmune process

shortlist.label: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and laboratory results could be consistent with a spondyloarthropathy, such as ankylosing spondylitis or psoriatic arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient developed knee pain and swelling shortly after receiving methotrexate, which is a known side effect of the medication, and the laboratory tests and joint ultrasonography findings are consistent with an inflammatory reaction

rejected.label: Reactive arthritis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of a preceding infection, which is typically required for reactive arthritis

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: The patient is afebrile and the laboratory tests do not suggest a bacterial infection

rejected.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
rejected.why: The onset of symptoms is too rapid and the patient's age and sex are not typical for rheumatoid arthritis

rejected.label: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of axial skeletal involvement or other characteristic features of seronegative spondyloarthropathy
